text:
Alex M: Heads up, saw a spike of NCCL job failures on g5-pool-5 starting ~08:12 UTC. Allreduce times out, processes stuck.
Nora L: Can you paste the job logs? which failures exactly?
Alex M: Main error is NCCL timeout, then kernel logs show: "mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: mlx5_comp: reg_mr failed: -12" and later "IBV_EVENT_QP_FATAL".
Samir: -12 is ENOMEM right? Could be memory region registration exhaustion. Any recent config changes?
Alex M: Not on our side. Node list: g5-11..g5-15 in eu-west-1. Affected 4/5 nodes.
InfraBot: Canary check: rdma ping between g5-11 -> g5-12 returned 0% loss but ibv_rc_pingpong times out intermittently.
Lee: I saw mlx5 driver oops in a cluster node earlier this week after the kernel patch roll. Hmm.
Marco P: Are these large collective ops? size of buffers?
Alex M: Yes, models are 70B sharded -> per-rank tensor >2GB; NCCL uses GPUDirect so we see large MR reg attempts.
Samir: Large MR + pinned memory pressure can hit reg_mr limits. Check /proc/sys/mlx5/qp/num_mr? (not exact path) Also check mlx5_core log for page pinning failures.
Nora L: Ran: dmesg snippet:
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: mlx5_comp: reg_mr failed: -12
[ 12345.678905] nv_peer_mem: failed to register memory: -12
[ 12345.678910] ibdev 1: QP fatal error, closing
```
Alex M: We haven't changed hugepage or pinning configs. We've pinned more GPUs recently due to capacity shuffle.
Lee: Quick mitigation: disable GPUDirect (nv_peer_mem) for the job so NCCL falls back to host copy. That doubles latency but unblocks.
Alex M: Can we roll that at scheduler level for eu-west batch queue? Add env NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME/ NCCL_P2P_LEVEL? Or set NV_PEER_MEM=0?
Samir: Env to disable peer memory is "NV_peer_mem" not standard. Quick approach: set "--gres=gpu:nn"? Not great. Better: module blacklist nv_peer_mem on those nodes temporarily.
Nora L: I pushed a canary: blacklisted nv_peer_mem on g5-12 only. Running the failing job now.
InfraBot: Canary result: job progressed past previous hang point, allreduce finished with TCP fallback, job completed albeit 2.1x slower.
Alex M: Good. Need root cause. Hypothesis: kernel patch changed page pinning or CMA handling causing reg_mr ENOMEM for >2GB MRs.
Marco P: Check /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages and VM settings (vm.max_map_count, memlock). Also check rdma-core and mlx5 driver versions across nodes.
Samir: Action items:
- Gather dmesg + mlx logs from all affected nodes (g5-11..15) — Samir
- Compare kernel + OFED versions across eu-west pool — Lee
- Try increasing pinned memory limits or tune vm.max_map_count on a test node — Nora
- Schedule driver rollback/patch test if mismatch found — Marco
Nora L: I'll also run a small repro: allocate contiguous 2.5GB GPU tensor and call ibv_reg_mr from userland to reproduce.
Alex M: ETA on repro? We need to decide whether to blacklist nv_peer_mem cluster-wide or only queue level.
Nora L: Repro in ~45m. If consistent, we should target a driver rollback and coordinate with infra for a maintenance window.
Samir: For short term, we'll keep nv_peer_mem blacklisted on affected nodes and add scheduler rule to prefer non-GPUDirect nodes for huge-shard jobs.
Lee: Also open ticket with NIC vendor with attached dmesg and ibv logs; requesting confirmation on reg_mr ENOMEM patterns after kernel x.y.z.
Alex M: Thanks team. Adding triage notes to incident tracker. @Marco P can you own vendor outreach?
Marco P: On it. I'll attach logs and repro steps once Nora has them.
Alex M: :thumbsup: Keep updates here.
